answer: A wharf authority resists Sybils by charging every agent a bonded reputation deposit before it may trade. A fresh identity starts on a small island of low-trust peers and reaches the main market only after its work is attested by established agents. Misbehaving identities lose their stake and become a relic: a public record of forfeited collateral that warns others. Attackers can spawn many identities, but each costs a real deposit plus weeks of attested work, so flooding the market costs more than any profit it could extract.
